elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, ..., circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}; several states may be displayed at once'. 'A steady red with a green turn arrow' is a head displaying circular_red (the steady red; flashing_red is a separate state) together with green_arrow(dir) for a turning dir ∈ {left, right, u_turn} (a straight arrow is no turn arrow), and not circular_green. 'The signal' of NRS 484B.307 is a signal by which traffic is controlled: dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', ties the head to a travel region g it controls; st.travel_region is the kind the quantifier over g ranges over (the abstract union of the kinds a device can govern).

'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed by id and never expanded.

'Facing such a signal': the same head h as s1 ('such a signal'). The head (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the subject's position (kin.position), and with D the vector from the subject's position to the head and H its heading (kin.heading, read normalised): H·D > 0 and (H·D)² ≥ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos²·|D|². The head's position is used for facing only, never as a stop line or crossing. The head faced is one controlling traffic at the place the pedestrian faces across: a travel region g it governs lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_governed_reach of the subject's body (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), which ties the head to the subject through the region it controls.

'Shall not enter the highway': a pedestrian facing the signal already stands on the highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines', sidewalks included). Entering is read as its footprint coming to overlap (rel.occupies) some st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic', having overlapped none at the previous observation.

'Unless permitted to proceed by another device as provided in NRS 484B.283' borrows the permissions NRS 484B.283(1)(d) sets forth. From NRS-484B-283-1d1: 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'; from NRS-484B-283-1d2: 'While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'. The other device is a pedestrian head d (dev.pedestrian_signal, state walk, or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute) governing (dev.governs) the roadway or lane r (st.roadway, st.lane) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), which anchors d to the subject; 'facing the signal' / 'in the direction of the signal' is the facing test on d (dev.position, kin.position, kin.heading) with p.ped_signal_facing_cos and p.ped_signal_facing_reach. From NRS-484B-283-1d3: 'a pedestrian who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) [NRS-484B-283-1d1] may continue to cross the highway'; from NRS-484B-283-1d4: 'a pedestrian who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) or (2) [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2] may continue to cross the highway': the subject's latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto a roadway or lane r' was made while a pedestrian head governing r' showed walk or dont_walk_flashing with countdown and the subject faced it, and its footprint has overlapped no sidewalk since. No rule of NRS 484B.283 is composed: the node of 283(1)(d)(1) is the drivers' duty to yield and those of (d)(3) and (d)(4) are prohibitions, none the pedestrian's permission.

compositions.quote: While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal
a pedestrian who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) [NRS-484B-283-1d1] may continue to cross the highway
a pedestrian who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) or (2) [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2] may continue to cross the highway

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian). At the judged observation there is a traffic signal head h (dev.traffic_signal) that shows circular_red and a green turn arrow (green_arrow(left), green_arrow(right) or green_arrow(u_turn)) and does not show circular_green; h governs (dev.governs) some travel region g whose ground distance from the subject's body (st.region_geometry) is at most p.ped_traffic_signal_governed_reach; and the subject faces h: with D the vector from the subject's kin.position to h's dev.position and H the subject's kin.heading, H·D > 0, (H·D)² ≥ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos² · (Dx² + Dy²), and Dx² + Dy² ≤ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach². Excepted (s5, permitted to proceed by another device as provided in NRS 484B.283): (a) there are a roadway or lane r (st.roadway or st.lane) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) and a pedestrian head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) governing r (dev.governs) that shows walk, or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute true, and the subject faces d (with Δ from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach²); or (b) the subject is continuing a crossing it entered lawfully under subparagraph (1) or (2): its latest step from a sidewalk onto a roadway or lane r' (its footprint coming to overlap r' while it overlapped a st.sidewalk at the previous observation) was made while a pedestrian head governing r' showed walk or dont_walk_flashing with countdown and the subject faced that head, and its footprint has overlapped no st.sidewalk since (since, past); where that step lies before the recording, (b) is unknown.
obligation: It is not the case that the subject's footprint overlaps some st.roadway region at the judged observation and overlapped no st.roadway region at the previous observation (it does not enter the roadway).

narrowings.why: A pedestrian facing the signal already stands on the highway (its sidewalk); entering the highway is read as entering the roadway, the part of the highway it is not yet on.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian stands on the sidewalk facing, within reach and within the facing angle, a head that governs the roadway beside it and displays circular_red with green_arrow(left); no pedestrian signal is present. The pedestrian steps into the roadway: its footprint comes to overlap a st.roadway region.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the pedestrian remains on the sidewalk while the head displays the red with the arrow.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head the pedestrian faces displays circular_green alone; it steps into the roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the head's position is not observed (dev.position absent), so whether the pedestrian faces it is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a pedestrian signal head across the crossing, governing the roadway the pedestrian steps onto and faced by it, displays walk: the pedestrian is permitted to proceed by another device.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in branch_1, but the pedestrian head displays dont_walk_steady: no device permits the pedestrian to proceed.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian stepped from the sidewalk onto the first roadway of a divided highway while a faced pedestrian head governing it showed walk, crosses the median without touching a sidewalk, and steps onto the second roadway while facing a vehicular head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(right) and the pedestrian head now shows dont_walk_flashing without countdown: it is continuing a crossing it entered lawfully.

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_governed_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest ground distance from a pedestrian's body to a travel region a vehicular signal head governs at which the head counts as controlling traffic at the place the pedestrian faces across: a wide urban intersection (about 40 m) plus the approach lanes beneath a far-side head beyond the far crosswalk
param_proposals.source: urban intersection dimensions and MUTCD far-side head placement
